text: Survivorship rules are the explicit, documented logic that decides which source wins for each attribute when building a golden record — not left to whoever happens to be merging the record that day.

Most recent wins — good for anything that changes over time, like a phone number. Trusted source wins — a specific system is authoritative for a specific attribute, like the ERP for billing address. Most complete wins — a populated value beats a blank one by default.

A blanket rule like 'the CRM always wins' usually breaks down — great for contact details sales reps update constantly, terrible for billing fields they never touch. Real survivorship logic is defined per attribute, not as one global rule for the whole record.

Phone number: most recent source wins. Legal address: trusted source, always the ERP. Segmentation field: most complete, since it's rarely filled in anywhere. Each attribute gets its own rule, written down.
Next: match review and stewardship — the human-in-the-loop step for the matches that don't resolve automatically, closing out this chapter.
